message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: NodeJS 20.x

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "master" ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [20.x]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        cache: npm

    - name: Install shared dependencies
      run: npm install --ignore-scripts

    - name: Build Core
      run: |
        cd ./packages/survey-core
        npm install
        npm run build:all

    - name: Build React UI
      run: |
        cd ./packages/survey-react-ui
        npm install
        npm run build

    - name: Build Angular UI
      run: |
        cd ./packages/survey-angular-ui
        npm install
        npm run build

    - name: Build Vue3 UI
      run: |
        cd ./packages/survey-vue3-ui
        npm install
        npm run build

    - name: Build JS UI
      run: |
        cd ./packages/survey-js-ui
        npm install
        npm run build
",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs npm install at the repository root and once inside each of five packages on every push to master, with no dependency cache, so repeated CI runs re-fetch the same packages. Evidence pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (dependency_cache) supports caching dependency downloads to cut repeated fetch time; its preconditions are met (repeated dependency fetching on a push schedule, lockfile/environment-keyed cache inputs available via npm) and no contraindications apply (no equivalent cache already exists; the npm cache is not mutable or untrusted content). The change is minimal-adding cache: npm to the existing setup-node step-and retains every install, build, and required check unchanged, with no new network access, secrets, or privileged actions.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
